question.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=xy+5x+{z}^{2}$, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,2)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,-1,2).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy+5x+{z}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy+5x+{z}^{2})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy+5x+{z}^{2})\,k \\  & =(y+5)\text{ }i+x\text{ }j+2z\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,-1,2) & =(-1+5)\,i+(1)\,j+2(2)\,k \\  & =4\,i+j+4\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $4\,i+j+4\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,2).$
